concepts.name: Alauddin Khalji's Market Reforms (Market Control System)
key_dimensions: Three-market structure: Grain market (Mandi), Cloth/cattle market (Sarai Adl), Cattle/horse/cattle market — purpose and distinctions
Administrative machinery: Shahna-i-Mandi, Barid (intelligence), Munhiyans (secret spies) — overlapping roles and UPSC trap on who reported what
Price fixation rationale — military efficiency vs. welfare debate among historians
Failure and dismantling after Alauddin's death — reasons and legacy

concepts.name: Token Currency Experiment under Muhammad bin Tughluq
key_dimensions: Distinction between brass/copper token and silver tanka — which replaced what and why it failed
Counterfeiting crisis and state's inability to control private minting — administrative loophole
Comparison with Alauddin's price control — both as economic interventions with contrasting outcomes
Historian debates: Ibn Battuta's account vs. modern economic interpretation of the policy

concepts.name: Iqta System and Its Economic Implications
key_dimensions: Iqta as revenue assignment vs. land grant — critical UPSC distinction (not hereditary, not zamindari)
Evolution from Iltutmish to later Sultans — how it changed from administrative tool to economic burden
Role of Muqti/Wali in revenue collection and surplus remittance to the centre
Alauddin's reform of Iqta — cash payment (waqf) vs. Iqta assignment: fiscal centralization angle

concepts.name: Agrarian Structure and Land Revenue under the Sultanate
key_dimensions: Kharaj (land tax on non-Muslims), Ushr (tithe on Muslims), Zakat — distinction and UPSC trap on who paid what
Measurement methods — lack of uniform measurement before Sher Shah; Sultanate reliance on estimation
Role of Khuts, Muqaddams, and Chaudharis as intermediaries — exploitation vs. facilitation debate
Alauddin's attempt to eliminate intermediary profits — impact on agrarian economy

concepts.name: Trade Routes and Commercial Geography of Sultanate Period
key_dimensions: Overland Silk Route connectivity — role of Delhi Sultanate in Central Asian trade
Indo-Arabian Sea trade routes — role of Gujarat and Malabar ports under Sultanate suzerainty
Shift of trade centres: Multan, Lahore, Delhi, Daulatabad — geographic significance
Impact of Mongol invasions on overland trade routes and merchant displacement into India

concepts.name: Role of Merchants and Trading Communities (Multanis, Sahus, Banjaras)
key_dimensions: Multani merchants as financiers of state grain procurement under Alauddin — public-private nexus
Banjaras as grain transporters — strategic military supply chain role often overlooked
Sahus and indigenous money-lenders vs. Muslim merchant guilds — coexistence and competition
UPSC trap: Banjaras' role in Alauddin's market system vs. their later role under Mughals

concepts.name: Currency System and Monetary Economy of the Sultanate
key_dimensions: Standardization of silver tanka by Iltutmish — foundational monetary reform
Bimetallic system: gold (dinar), silver (tanka), copper (jital) — which was dominant and why
Debasement of coinage in later Sultanate period (Firuz Shah Tughluq era) — fiscal stress indicator
Comparison between Sultanate coinage and Mughal monetary reforms — continuity vs. change

concepts.name: Taxation System Beyond Land Revenue (Non-Agrarian Taxes)
key_dimensions: Jizya — on whom levied, exemptions, and UPSC trap: was it always collected throughout Sultanate period?
Octroi/transit duties (rahdari) and their impact on internal trade
Ghari (house tax) and Charai (pasture tax) introduced by Alauddin — novelty and resistance
Firuz Shah Tughluq's restoration of Jizya on Brahmins — policy reversal significance

concepts.name: Firuz Shah Tughluq's Economic and Fiscal Policies
key_dimensions: Abolition of illegal taxes vs. introduction of new cesses — net fiscal impact debate
Canal irrigation projects as state investment in agrarian economy — Nahr-i-Firuz and others
Decentralization of Iqta and its long-term weakening of central revenue
Welfare expenditure (hospitals, rest houses) vs. fiscal imprudence — historian disagreement

concepts.name: Urban Economy and Craft Production under the Sultanate
key_dimensions: Royal karkhanas (workshops) — state-controlled production vs. market economy
Textile industry: silk, cotton, muslin production centres and their trade significance
Artisan guilds (shrenis) — continuity from pre-Sultanate period or disruption?
UPSC trap: karkhanas as wage-labour institutions vs. slave-labour institutions — Barani's account

concepts.name: Imports, Exports, and Balance of Trade under the Sultanate
key_dimensions: Key imports: horses, gold, luxury goods — strategic and economic dimensions
Key exports: textiles, spices (via southern trade), indigo — regional production centres
Horse trade monopoly and military-economic nexus — why horse import was a strategic vulnerability
Role of Arab and Chinese merchants in Indian Ocean trade during Sultanate period

concepts.name: Impact of Mongol Invasions on Sultanate Economy
key_dimensions: Disruption of Central Asian overland trade routes — displacement of merchants into India as a positive side-effect
Military expenditure surge under Alauddin to fund anti-Mongol campaigns — link to market reforms
Demographic and agrarian disruption in Punjab and northwestern regions
Influx of skilled craftsmen and scholars fleeing Mongols — cultural-economic stimulus

concepts.name: Role of Sufis and Religious Establishments in Sultanate Economy
key_dimensions: Waqf (religious endowments) as economic institutions — land revenue diversion from state
Khanqahs as nodes of redistribution — feeding the poor and economic function
UPSC trap: Waqf under Sultanate vs. Waqf under Mughals — scale and state control differences

concepts.name: Deccan and Southern Campaigns — Economic Motivations and Consequences
key_dimensions: Plunder economy vs. administrative integration — which model did Sultans actually follow?
Alauddin's Deccan campaigns (Malik Kafur) — tribute extraction and its one-time vs. recurring nature
Muhammad bin Tughluq's Daulatabad transfer — economic rationale and failure

concepts.name: Slave Economy and Forced Labour under the Sultanate
key_dimensions: Firuz Shah Tughluq's slave corps (180,000 slaves) — largest in Sultanate history and its fiscal burden
Slaves in karkhanas vs. slaves in military service — economic vs. military function distinction

concepts.name: Price Revolution and Inflation in the Later Sultanate Period
key_dimensions: Post-Alauddin price decontrol — rapid inflation as evidence of artificial suppression earlier
Muhammad bin Tughluq's currency experiment causing inflation — mechanism and historical evidence
Firuz Shah era: relative price stability due to decentralization or due to reduced military demand?

concepts.name: Gujarat and Coastal Trade Economies under Sultanate Suzerainty
key_dimensions: Gujarat's semi-autonomous status and its role as premier trade entrepôt
Cambay (Khambhat) port — Arab, Persian, Chinese merchant presence and commodity exchange
Sultanate's limited naval capacity and dependence on merchant communities for maritime trade
Incorporation of Gujarat into Delhi Sultanate under Alauddin — economic vs. strategic motivation

concepts.name: Economic Causes of the Decline of the Delhi Sultanate
key_dimensions: Revenue decentralization through Iqta proliferation under Firuz Shah — structural fiscal weakening
Timur's invasion (1398) — destruction of Delhi's commercial and artisan base
Failure of agricultural taxation reforms to keep pace with military expenditure growth
Rise of regional sultanates (Bahmani, Bengal, Malwa) as economic secession from Delhi's revenue system
